note: Stolerman et al. (2019) and subsequent studies establish KDM6B-associated neurodevelopmental syndrome characterized by developmental delay, ID, speech impairment, behavioral features, and facial dysmorphisms.

evidence.text: Stolerman et al. identified de novo alterations in KDM6B associated with developmental delay, intellectual disability, dysmorphic facial features, and other clinical findings.

source.title: Genetic variants in the KDM6B gene are associated with neurodevelopmental delays and dysmorphic features
source.quote: We have identified a number of de novo alterations in the KDM6B gene via whole exome sequencing (WES) in a cohort of 12 unrelated patients with developmental delay, intellectual disability, dysmorphic facial features, and other clinical findings.
